newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo has no plans for other major sales.
newsitem.headline: Anglo has no plans for other major sales.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd chairman Julian Ogilvie Thompson said on Tuesday that Anglo had no plans to dispose of any other assets the size of its JCI and Johnnic stakes.
"We don't have any plans along those lines...The main thrust in these cases is to make our contribution to black empowerment," Ogilvie Thompson said.
Anglo recently disposed of its 35 percent stake in Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd (Johnnic) to the National Empowerment Consortium, a black business grouping.
On Tuesday Anglo announced the sale of its 34.9 percent stake in JCI to black empowerment group Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd.
Anglo said it hoped to win 2.1 billion rand from the sale of its Johnnic stake.
Asked whether the group planned to take the 2.1 billion rand out of the country, Ogilvie Thompson said that this was unlikely due to South Africa's current foreign exchange controls.
"I don't think we can expect a significant softening in exchange control rules in the immediate future," he said.
He said that Anglo had a number of ongoing projects within South Africa in which the money could be invested.
